title: create_group and add_member: one transaction per use case
problem: Write two use cases with the SQLAlchemy ORM. create_group creates a chat with its members, all or nothing. add_member adds one user to an existing chat and reports whether anything changed. Each function opens and commits its own transaction from the session factory it receives.
requirements: Each function uses one transaction from session_factory, committed on success and rolled back on any error
create_group: unknown usernames raise LookupError naming them, and nothing is saved
create_group: a blank or whitespace-only title raises ValueError, and nothing is saved
create_group: the creator and members are added once each, even if repeated; return the new chat id
add_member: True if added, False if already a member; LookupError for an unknown chat or user
contract: create_group(session_factory, title, creator, members) -> int; add_member(session_factory, chat_id, username) -> bool
expectedBehavior: create_group(factory, 'backend', 'ali', ['sara', 'omid']) returns an id whose members are ali, omid and sara; create_group(factory, 'x', 'ali', ['ghost']) raises LookupError and leaves no chat behind
edgeCases: Duplicates, including the creator in members
hints: Conceptual: put the whole use case inside `with session_factory.begin() as session:`. An exception raised inside the block rolls back everything, so validate and raise freely.

Specific: load all users with one select(User).where(User.username.in_(names)) and compare with the names you asked for. You need the chat's id before creating ChatMember rows; session.flush() sends the INSERT without committing.

Implementation: dedupe with list(dict.fromkeys([creator, *members])); after session.add(chat) and session.flush(), add one ChatMember(chat_id=chat.id, user_id=...) per user and return chat.id inside the with block. For add_member, session.get(ChatMember, (chat_id, user_id)) checks membership.
evaluation: No commit() or rollback() calls scattered through the code: the begin() block owns the transaction
One query for all usernames, not one per name
